transcripts.transcript:
Good afternoon, Helen Tan. This is Daniel Lim for our scheduled portfolio review. Is this still a convenient time to speak?

Good afternoon, Daniel Lim. Yes, I have my paperwork beside me and somewhere quiet to sit. My identification number is F zero one six six nine five eight H. My date of birth is the second of August nineteen sixty-five.

Thank you. Before we get into the review, how is your gardening project coming along?

The planting is finished, although the clearing up seems to take longer than the gardening. It has been a pleasant change from sitting indoors with paperwork.

It sounds as though it has kept you occupied. Would you prefer to keep using telephone appointments for your portfolio reviews?

Yes, telephone appointments are easier. I can spread the papers out at home without having to bring them into the branch. I would rather keep the conversation fairly concise, though.

Certainly. I'll keep the discussion focused and leave room for any questions you want to raise.

Looking through my portfolio for this review, there is Orion Global Income Fund to consider. Then there is my holding in Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 to consider as well. For this transaction, I choose the second holding I mentioned.

Your objective is to reduce your exposure to this issuer and make part of your invested wealth more readily available for personal spending.

I have the relevant page open now. I made some notes before the call so that I wouldn't have to search through everything while we talked.

I recommend reducing your holding in Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 to lower your concentration in this issuer and release money for personal spending. A sell limit would set a minimum acceptable execution price, although it would not ensure a sale.

There is something I would like to ask before we get into the details. If I keep holding the bond instead, can you guarantee its future returns?

No, I cannot guarantee future returns from holding the bond. For Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, limited secondary-market liquidity can make it difficult to find a buyer. A sell limit order may remain unfilled if buyers will not meet your minimum price. Do you understand that limited liquidity could prevent a sale and that your limit order could remain unfilled?

Yes, I understand: there may not be a buyer willing to meet my limit, so the holding might remain unsold.

The transaction fee is 0.25%. You may lose some or all of the capital invested in this bond. Selling below what you paid would crystallise a capital loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss, including a loss crystallised by selling, in order to reduce your exposure?

Yes, I am willing to accept an investment loss from selling to reduce my exposure to this issuer.

We can now turn to the proposed order details. I'll listen while you refer to your notes.

I want to sell from my existing holding. The transaction currency should be American dollars. The amount for this transaction is 25,000. The quantity I want to transact is 250 units. Please use a limit order with a limit price of 100 American dollars.

To recap, you wish to sell 250 units of Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, with a transaction amount of 25,000 in American dollars, using a limit order at 100 American dollars. Do you explicitly confirm this final instruction?

Mm, I hear you. Let me think about that for a moment.

Take your time. There is no need to fill the silence while you consider it.

Thank you. I'd prefer to leave the conversation there for now and sit quietly with my notes.

Of course. Thank you for your time today, Helen Tan. Goodbye.

Goodbye, Daniel Lim.
